correctness.rationale: The intersection recurrence produces all six distance polynomials and the exact seven adjacency eigenvalues. On the zero-sum space, the bipartition spectral branch \(F(p)\) has \(F(0)=-1\), derivative \(>0.179q^5\) and second derivative \(<7q^5\) on \([0,10/q^5]\). Thus it has one zero. All five other spectral modes remain below -0.96 by a uniform \(\le4000q^{-5/2}\) deviation bound. Schoenberg monotonicity supplies the full exponent range. Inverting the derivative with controlled Taylor remainder gives the two-term expansion; simple bipartition eigenvalue and Gram rank establish the equality-space/dimension claims. A standard-library checker verifies polynomial recurrences and sample spectra but does not stand in for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The incidence metrics of equal-order generalized hexagons constitute a natural infinite family with diameter six and unbounded size. The theorem evaluates their exact Hilbert-snowflake threshold for all sufficiently large admissible orders and reveals a sharp \(q^{-5}\) scale, explicit two-term coefficients, a unique spectral obstruction, and a one-dimensional critical Gram-rank drop. These quantitative structural conclusions are not provided by a generic graph-spectrum algorithm or by finite small-graph checks; extensions to small orders or other polygons are not needed for the claimed value.
